"Hajj is Arafah", and tawaf al-ifadah is commanded in the Quran. Most schools also count ihram and sa'i as pillars (for Hanafis ihram is a condition and sa'i a wajib), and Shafi'is add the shave or trim.
"Hajj is Arafah." Being there — on the {1}th, or in the night before Fajr of the {2}th — is the pillar without which there is no Hajj.
"The days of tashreeq are days of eating, drinking and the remembrance of Allah" — the "numbered days" of Quran {1}.

"Whoever forgets something of his rites or leaves it out, let him shed blood" (Ibn Abbas). A missed wajib is repaired with a dam; a missed pillar is not — it must be done. Which rites are wajib differs a little between the schools, so learn your group's list.
False — "I stood here, and all of Arafah is a place of standing." Sitting in your tent inside the boundary counts in full; climbing the hill is not a rite.
False — Hajj adds Arafat, Muzdalifah, Mina and the fixed days of Dhul-Hijjah; Umrah is ihram, tawaf, sa'i and halq.

False — a child's Hajj is valid: when a woman held up a child and asked "Is there Hajj for this one?", the Prophet ﷺ said "Yes, and you will have a reward." But the scholars agree he must perform it again after puberty to fulfil the obligation.
From the {1}th (Tarwiyah) to the {2}th — or the {3}th if you stay in Mina. The {4}th is Arafah and the {5}th is Eid al-Adha.

He led Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha and Fajr in Mina, then waited for sunrise before moving on. The four-rakah prayers were shortened to two; whether a pilgrim who has stayed long in Makkah also shortens differs between the schools.

He stoned on the {1}th in the forenoon, and afterwards "when the sun had declined." Ibn Umar: "We used to wait till the sun declined." Whether you may stone after sunset differs: Hanafis and Shafi'is allow it, and the Saudi fatwa bodies follow this; the Hanbali school moves it to the next day after midday — follow your group.
Ihram at the miqat, then tawaf, then sa'i, then cutting the hair — in that order.
Once in a lifetime. When a man asked "every year?", the Prophet ﷺ said: "If I said yes, it would become obligatory — and you would not be able to do it."

One adhan, two iqamahs, nothing prayed between them — then the standing began. That is the Sunnah and the majority practice; Abu Hanifa allowed the combining only behind the imam, so many Hanafi groups pray each in its own time in the tents, and the schools differ on who shortens — follow your group's scholar.
Seven rounds, counter-clockwise, starting and ending at the Black Stone corner.
Seven, one at a time, with a takbir for each.
Takbir with each pebble, then a long dua facing the qibla after the small and the middle — and none after Aqabah.
The small one by Masjid al-Khayf, then the middle, then Aqabah — "I saw the Prophet ﷺ doing like this." Most scholars make this order a condition; Hanafis hold it is a sunnah.

True — unlike Hajj, Umrah has no fixed date. (Ramadan carries a special reward.) Hanafis dislike it on {1}–{2} Dhul Hijjah, and Saudi authorities pause Umrah permits around the Hajj season — check Nusuk for your dates.
Umrah is the "minor pilgrimage" — Hajj is the major one with fixed dates and extra rites.
Yawm at-Tarwiyah — the day the companions set out for Mina in ihram for Hajj. The {1}th is Arafah, the {2}th the Day of Nahr, and the {3}th the Day of Qarr (staying).
